extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is a comprehensive multi-modal evaluation benchmark for MLLMs in video analysis, featuring 900 videos across 6 visual domains with 30 subfields, 2,700 multiple-choice questions, and multi-modal inputs including subtitles and audios. Videos range from 11 seconds to 1 hour in duration, covering short-, medium-, and long-term temporal contexts.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 finely-grained video categories. Videos of varying durations (short <2 min, medium 4-15 min, long 30-60 min) were collected along with subtitles and audio metadata. Question-answer pairs were manually annotated by annotators with strong English proficiency and research experience in vision-language learning, followed by a rigorous quality review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 900 videos sourced from YouTube across 6 domains and 30 categories, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audio, spanning short (<2 min), medium (4-15 min), and long (30-60 min) durations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning watched entire videos and created 3 multiple-choice QA pairs each (4 candidate options per question). Each QA pair was then reviewed by a different annotator for clarity, answerability, and correctness. QA pairs answerable without video were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro in a text-only setup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in a text-only setup, confirming that QA pairs require video content to answer. Answer option distribution is near-uniform (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 QA pairs per video, with each QA pair reviewed by a second annotator
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to filter out QA pairs answerable from text alone (without video)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset reflects a long-tailed distribution of complex temporal reasoning data, which poses challenges for acquisition and may introduce bias toward simpler or shorter video content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Performance declines as video duration increases; open-source models face restricted input frames as an information bottleneck for long videos. Availability of datasets with complex temporal reasoning in long videos remains limited compared to text and image datasets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to inspire future research and development in improving the capabilities of MLLMs for video understanding, potentially advancing AI systems that can better understand long sequential world dynamics.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating (benchmarking) MLLMs on video understanding tasks, including temporal reasoning. It can also be used to guide instruction-tuning dataset construction for complex temporal understanding in long videos.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: QA pairs that could be answered without video content were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro in text-only setup; answer options follow near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%) to ensure unbiased evaluation; videos collected with balanced distribution across short, medium, and long durations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos collected from YouTube across 6 domains and 30 categories with varying durations (short <2 min, medium 4-15 min, long 30-60 min); meta-information including subtitles and audio obtained; QA pairs annotated in multiple-choice format with 4 candidate options; manual review conducted to verify clarity, answerability, and correctness of QA pairs.
